s: Solomon asks God for wisdom and receives riches and honour as well.
Solomon prepares to build the temple and asks Hiram of Tyre for help.
Solomon builds the temple on Mount Moriah.
The temple furnishings are made.
The ark is brought into the temple, and the glory of the Lord fills the house as a cloud.
Solomon's prayer of dedication.
Fire falls from heaven on the sacrifices. God promises to hear his people if they humble themselves and pray.
Solomon's building works and his trade by sea.
The queen of Sheba visits. Solomon's wealth and his death.
The kingdom divides when Rehoboam refuses to lighten the people's burden.
Rehoboam fortifies Judah, and faithful priests and Levites come to him from the north.
Rehoboam abandons the law, and Egypt's king plunders Jerusalem.
King Abijah defeats Jeroboam because Judah relies on the Lord.
King Asa removes idols and trusts God, who defeats a great Ethiopian army.
Azariah encourages Asa, and Judah renews its covenant with the Lord.
Asa relies on Syria instead of God and is rebuked.
Jehoshaphat strengthens Judah and sends teachers through the land with the book of the law.
Jehoshaphat allies with Ahab, and the prophet Micaiah foretells disaster.
Jehoshaphat appoints judges and tells them to judge in the fear of the Lord.
A great army comes against Judah. Jehoshaphat prays, the people sing praise, and God defeats the enemy.
King Jehoram does evil and dies of a terrible disease.
Athaliah seizes the throne and kills the royal family, but the boy Joash is hidden.
The priest Jehoiada crowns Joash and Athaliah is killed.
Joash repairs the temple, but after Jehoiada dies he turns away and kills Zechariah the priest.
King Amaziah's victory over Edom, his idolatry, and his defeat.
King Uzziah prospers until pride leads him to burn incense in the temple, and he is struck with leprosy.
King Jotham grows strong because he walks before the Lord.
King Ahaz worships other gods and closes the temple. Judah suffers defeat.
Hezekiah reopens and cleanses the temple and restores its worship.
Hezekiah invites all Israel and Judah to a great Passover in Jerusalem.
The people destroy idols and bring offerings to the temple in abundance.
Sennacherib of Assyria invades. Hezekiah and Isaiah pray, and an angel destroys the Assyrian army.
Manasseh does great evil, is taken captive, repents and is restored. Amon reigns.
Josiah seeks God from his youth and repairs the temple, where the book of the law is found.
Josiah keeps a great Passover. He dies in battle with Egypt and Jeremiah laments him.
The last kings of Judah. Jerusalem falls to Babylon, and the exile lasts until Cyrus of Persia lets the people return.
